---
title: Architecture
description: How NCBI feeds become the public Parquet files. Scheduled extracts, an internal DuckLake, SQLMesh marts, and a nightly export.
---

OmicIDX is a batch pipeline. Every job is a plain Python process run by a
systemd timer. There's no orchestrator and no database serving the public.

```
NCBI FTP / E-utilities
        │   per-source extracts, one systemd timer each
        ▼
raw Parquet / NDJSON on Cloudflare R2
        │   nightly: MERGE into the lake
        ▼
internal DuckLake (Postgres catalog, data on R2)
        │   SQLMesh: staging → sradb / geometadb marts
        ▼
nightly Parquet export ──▶ omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/
                              latest/, v{date}/
                                │ monthly
                                ▼
                         HuggingFace seandavis/omicidx (tagged, DOI)
```

## Stages

1. **Extract.** One job per source (SRA, GEO, BioSample/BioProject, PubMed, and EBI BioSamples) downloads new upstream data and writes raw files to R2. A small marker file records each finished partition, so a failed job resumes where it stopped. Parsing uses [`omicidx-parsers`](https://github.com/seandavi/omicidx/tree/main/packages/omicidx-parsers).
2. **Load.** Every night, the raw files are merged into an internal [DuckLake](https://ducklake.select/) (Postgres catalog, Parquet data on R2). The lake keeps snapshots, so earlier states can be reproduced.
3. **Transform.** [SQLMesh](https://sqlmesh.com/) builds the `sradb` and `geometadb` marts from the lake tables.
4. **Publish.** The base tables and marts are exported to public Parquet: a new `v{date}/` folder, a refreshed `latest/`, an `omicidx.duckdb` of views, `views.sql`, `restore.sql` (a local-copy script), and `manifest.json`. A monthly job copies one release to HuggingFace.

Extraction and publishing are decoupled. The nightly build uses whatever raw
data is already on R2, so a slow or failing source only delays its own tables.

## Provenance

Each release's `manifest.json` records the publish date, the git commit of the
transform code (`transform_sha`), the internal lake snapshot it was exported
from (`lake_snapshot_id`), and per-table row counts. See [Versions and
citation](../guides/versions-and-citation.qmd).

## Source code

Everything is in [github.com/seandavi/omicidx](https://github.com/seandavi/omicidx):
parsers in `packages/omicidx-parsers`, the pipeline in
`packages/omicidx-prefect`, and the systemd units in `systemd/`.
